title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 112
paragraphs: On that day the Ionians for their part greatly distinguished themselves and overcame the Phoenicians, and of them the Samians were best. Meanwhile on land, when the armies met, they came to close quarters and fought; and as regards the two commanders, what happened was this: when Artybius came riding on his horse to fight with Onesilus, Onesilus, as he had arranged with his shield-bearer, struck at Artybius himself when he came to fight with him; and when the horse set its hooves against Onesilus's shield, then the Carian struck with a curved blade and cut off the horse's feet.
